title: Immediate Ambulatory Electrocardiographic Monitoring in Syncope
Zomato and District: strategic expansion into India’s event ticketing ecosystem
abstract: Learning outcomes After completion of the case study, the students will be able to: Case overview/synopsis This case examines a strategic dilemma faced by Deepinder Goyal, chief executive officer of Zomato, following the company’s 2024 acquisition of Paytm Insider and the launch of its event-ticketing platform, District. As Zomato expanded beyond food delivery into the live entertainment ecosystem, Goyal had to decide whether District should be aggressively scaled to directly challenge the incumbent BookMyShow, selectively grown as a complementary extension of Zomato’s ecosystem or limited to avoid strategic overextension. The case situates this decision within the broader context of platform-based competition, and acquisition-led diversification. Students are required to evaluate industry attractiveness, assess Zomato’s resource capabilities and analyze the trade-offs between growth, profitability and operational complexity. The case highlights the strategic challenges of entering a market dominated by a strong incumbent while managing risks related to financial sustainability, customer trust and organizational focus. Students are invited to analyze the competitive dynamics of the Indian ticketing industry, assess Zomato’s firm-specific resources and ecosystem advantages and evaluate the trade-offs between growth ambitions and long-term sustainability. The case encourages application of strategic frameworks to understand how platform-based firms navigate expansion into adjacent markets characterized by strong incumbents and trust-related challenges. Complexity academic level This case is most suitable for Master of Business Administration students or executive education participants enrolled in courses on strategic management, corporate strategy or marketing strategy. The case challenges students to think critically about how a technology-driven company like Zomato navigates diversification, digital ecosystem building and competitive positioning in a fast-evolving consumer market. It is most appropriate for participants with prior exposure to strategic analysis frameworks such as Porter’s five forces and the resource-based view. Subject code CSS11: Strategy.

title: Waste-derived feedstocks and industrial microwave drying influence antioxidant capacity and immune-associated protein composition in black soldier fly larvae (Hermetia illucens)
journal: Journal of Insects as Food and Feed
abstract: Abstract Black soldier fly larvae ( Hermetia illucens ) are increasingly used as a sustainable protein source in animal feeds. Beyond macronutrient value, black soldier fly larvae (BSFL) contain antioxidant compounds and immune-associated proteins that may contribute to their functional value. However, the extent to which rearing substrate and processing influence these components remains poorly understood. This study investigated the effects of feedstock and industrial microwave drying on antioxidant capacity and immune-associated protein composition in BSFL. Larvae were reared on three waste-derived feedstocks (fruit and vegetable waste, soy okara and brewer’s spent grain). Antioxidant capacity was measured using Folin-Ciocalteu, FRAP and DPPH assays. Immune-associated proteins and AMP candidates were characterised using LC-MS/MS proteomics. Industrial microwave drying was evaluated relative to freeze-drying. Antioxidant capacity differed significantly among feedstocks (ANOVA, ). Brewer’s spent grain increased total phenolic content and reducing capacity, while fruit and vegetable waste resulted in the highest radical scavenging activity. Total immune protein richness did not differ among diets; however, immune functional composition varied significantly (PERMANOVA, R 2 = 0.907, ). Larvae reared on fruit and vegetable waste showed increased representation of immune effector proteins and higher AMP candidate richness. Industrial microwave drying resulted in a 43% reduction in detectable immune-associated proteins and reduced antioxidant capacity. These findings demonstrate that feedstock and processing shape the composition and detectability of antioxidant and immune-associated components in BSFL biomass, highlighting opportunities to optimise insect-derived feed ingredients for targeted applications.

title: Unmet demand for flexibility: remote work preferences of office workers in Poland
abstract: Purpose Remote-work preferences are usually explained either by what jobs technically permit or by workers' household circumstances. This study proposes a third reading, in which preferences reflect a worker's position in an ongoing negotiation over flexibility, and tests it against a needs account using original survey data on office workers in Poland. Design/methodology/approach An original survey of 639 office workers in Polish cities of over 100,000 inhabitants, fielded in June 2024 once post-pandemic attitudes had stabilized. Ordinal logistic regression relates stated preferences to socio-demographic, employment-related, and experiential factors, entered jointly, allowing their relative weights to be compared directly; a partial proportional odds model then tests whether the same factors govern the move from office-based to hybrid work and from hybrid to fully remote work. Findings Preferences align with position within the employment relationship rather than household need: ownership and tenure predict strongly, while gender, education, and children do not; age is the sole demographic exception. Lived experience, especially perceived gains in non-work-life quality, is the strongest predictor, but its effect is asymmetric. It determines whether workers want any remote work far more than whether they want all of it, which makes hybrid work a distinct settlement rather than a stepping stone. The apparent gender gap is fully explained by differences in reported experience, and unmet demand is concentrated almost entirely among fully on-site workers. Originality/value Where prior Polish studies examine single channels in isolation, this study models three channels jointly: the socio-demographic, the employment-related, and the experiential. This provides novel evidence from Central and Eastern Europe. Theoretically, it turns negotiated flexibility from a framing device into a testable claim and finds evidence consistent with it: demand tracks the discretion workers hold more closely than it tracks their household needs. In a dependent market economy without sectoral bargaining, the resulting shortfall is best read as the residue of an unresolved negotiation.

title: Unlocking Literacy: The Role of Reading and Writing Skills in Shaping Elementary Learners’ Development
journal: International Journal of Transformative Multidisciplinary Studies
abstract: This study examined the reported levels of reading skills, writing skills, academic success, and challenges in literacy development among Grade 5 and Grade 6 learners. The study was conducted in selected public elementary schools in Lutayan, Sultan Kudarat during the School Year 2025–2026. A quantitative descriptive-correlational research design was employed. The respondents were 56 learners selected through proportionate sampling. Data were collected using a researcher-developed 40-item questionnaire covering reading skills (comprehension, vocabulary, and fluency); writing skills (syntax, grammar, and morphology); academic success; and challenges in reading and writing. The instrument obtained a mean validity score of 4.36 and a Cronbach’s alpha of 0.762, indicating acceptable internal consistency. Mean, standard deviation, and Pearson Product-Moment Correlation Coefficient were used to analyze the data. The findings showed that learners reported a very high level of reading skills (M = 4.40) and writing skills (M = 4.51). Academic success was reported as Very Satisfactory (M = 4.50), while challenges in developing literacy skills were reported as Challenged (M = 3.71). The correlation analysis showed a negligible positive relationship between reading skills and academic success (r = 0.119) and a negligible negative relationship between writing skills and academic success (r = -0.097). Neither relationship was statistically significant at the 0.05 level. The findings suggest that although learners reported high levels of reading and writing skills, these skills alone were not significantly related to their reported academic success. Other factors may also contribute to learners’ academic development.

title: The algorithmic mirror: AI disinhibition and anxiety-driven compensatory consumption
abstract: Purpose Consumers are increasingly exposed to AI influencers across digital marketing environments, yet little is known about how these virtual agents shape anxiety-driven purchasing behavior. This study aims to propose the AI disinhibition effect, a dual pathway model in which appearance anxiety drives consumption through a fear of missing out (FOMO)-mediated compensatory route common to all influencer types and a direct disinhibitory route unique to AI contexts where social evaluation is absent. Design/methodology/approach Four experimental studies expose participants to human, realistic AI or animated AI influencers presenting products at varying risk levels. Conditional process analyses examine the mediating role of FOMO and the moderating roles of influencer type, visual realism and product risk. Findings Appearance anxiety increases FOMO, which drives compensatory consumption across all influencer types. A direct anxiety to impulsive and compulsive buying pathways additionally emerges in AI contexts, where the absence of social evaluation reduces self-regulatory restraint. This disinhibitory effect is stronger for animated than realistic AI influencers and diminishes as product risk increases, disappearing entirely for high-risk categories where safety concerns restore deliberative processing. Research limitations/implications The studies rely on experimental stimuli and short-term behavioral intentions, suggesting opportunities for longitudinal and field-based extensions. Practical implications AI influencers are most effective for low-risk, identity-expressive categories such as fashion and beauty and considerably less so in high-risk categories such as health or financial products, where consumers engage greater scrutiny. Social implications By identifying conditions under which AI influencer environments amplify anxiety-driven consumption while bypassing deliberative control, this research raises important concerns for consumer well-being and highlights the ethical responsibilities of firms deploying virtual agents in marketing practice. Originality/value This research introduces the AI disinhibition effect and integrates it with compensatory consumption theory. It advances understanding of how influencer type, visual realism and product risk jointly shape anxiety-driven purchasing in AI-mediated marketing environments.

title: The Role of Schadenfreude in Judgments of Deserved Treatment toward Free Riders: Focusing on Cooperative Situations between Two Parties フリーライダーの処遇判断におけるシャーデンフロイデの役割――2者間の協力場面に着目して
Sistem Penilaian Kinerja Pegawai Teladan Berbasis Web Studi Kasus Badan Pusat Statistik Kabupaten Jombang
journal: DERISTECH : Development informatic and research in Technology
abstract: Kinerja pegawai merupakan unsur krusial dalam menentukan keberhasilan dan mutu pelayanan suatu instansi pemerintah. Di Badan Pusat Statistik (BPS) Kabupaten Jombang, proses penilaian pegawai teladan masih dilakukan secara manual melalui rekapitulasi berbasis spreadsheet. Pendekatan ini memiliki beberapa keterbatasan, antara lain risiko kesalahan perhitungan, pengolahan data yang tidak efisien, serta kurangnya transparansi dan optimalisasi. Oleh karena itu, diperlukan suatu sistem yang dapat mempercepat, mengobjektifikasi, dan menstrukturkan proses evaluasi. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk merancang dan mengembangkan sistem penilaian kinerja pegawai teladan berbasis web dengan menggunakan framework Flask dan basis data MySQL. Metode pengembangan yang diterapkan adalah model Waterfall yang meliputi tahapan analisis, perancangan, implementasi, pengujian, dan evaluasi. Sistem yang dikembangkan menyediakan fitur-fitur seperti pengelolaan data pegawai, input nilai berdasarkan kriteria, perhitungan skor otomatis dengan bobot tertentu, perangkingan pegawai, dan pembuatan sertifikat dalam format PDF. Pengujian melalui Black Box Testing menunjukkan bahwa seluruh fungsi sistem beroperasi dengan baik sesuai dengan kebutuhan pengguna. Sistem ini berkontribusi dalam meningkatkan efektivitas proses evaluasi dan mendukung transparansi dalam pemilihan pegawai teladan di BPS Kabupaten Jombang.

title: Knowledge flows and knowledge management in a public research center: an empirical study
journal: VINE Journal of Information and Knowledge Management Systems
abstract: Purpose This research aims to examine how knowledge flows circulate within a public innovation unit, how multidisciplinary teams interact and what these dynamics reveal about knowledge management (KM) maturity. Design/methodology/approach A survey-based case study with embedded qualitative responses was conducted at CeMEPI-PGE. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire administered to researchers from different teams. Closed-ended responses were analyzed using descriptive statistics, while open-ended responses were examined through thematic content analysis. Findings Semantic knowledge boundaries emerged as the most salient perceived integration barrier among the dimensions assessed, although collaborative potential remained high. Research limitations/implications The study is limited to a single case and relies primarily on questionnaire data, which restricts statistical generalization. Future research could adopt longitudinal and comparative designs to examine the evolution of KM maturity in emerging public innovation units. Practical implications The findings highlight the importance of strengthening knowledge governance through structured repositories, standardized documentation practices and institutionalized knowledge-sharing routines. Social implications Strengthening KM in public organizations contributes to improving the quality of public decision-making and the effectiveness of institutional innovation initiatives. By promoting better knowledge integration, organizational learning and preservation of institutional memory, KM practices can support more transparent, efficient and evidence-based public administration. In contexts such as public research and innovation centers, improved knowledge flows may enhance the State’s capacity to design and implement policies, optimize public resources and expand access to justice and public services. Originality/value This study contributes to the KM literature by proposing an interpretive lens through which early-stage maturity in newly created organizations may be understood in relation to institutional newness rather than solely as organizational deficiency. It also extends knowledge-boundary theory to multidisciplinary public research and innovation environments.
